compatibility.note: The spec tracks Charon main, so it can specify behaviour no final Charon release carries. A behaviour with a null first_charon_release is in no final release — only on main or in release candidates; its note says which. Compare against your Charon using first_charon_release_semver, the [major, minor, patch] triple: Charon's tags are not ordered by string comparison, so "v1.11.0" sorts below "v1.9.0".

behaviours.name: Deterministic (genesis-derived) eager double linear round deadlines
Extended 1.5s proposer round-1 timeout (proposal_timeout)
behaviours.note: The behaviour itself is older (charon #3739) but sat behind the alpha proposal_timeout feature flag; v1.9.0 (charon #4296) enabled it by default. The timer_deadlines vectors assume it is enabled.

behaviours.name: Linear round timer subsequent-round timeout fix
behaviours.note: No final Charon release carries this; it shipped in the v1.11.0 release candidates (first in v1.11.0-rc1). Timing-only, no wire change: against an older peer, its rounds 2+ simply time out on the uncorrected schedule.

behaviours.name: QBFT DECIDED-resend rate limit and message size/count limits
behaviours.note: No final Charon release carries this; it shipped in the v1.11.0 release candidates (first in v1.11.0-rc1). The limits only reject messages no honest peer sends, so enforcing them interoperates with every release.

behaviours.name: Preferred priority protocol ID /charon/priority/2.0.0
behaviours.note: Unreleased on Charon main. The legacy no-slash ID is the only one every released Charon speaks and must still be served; Charon targets v1.12 for the preferred ID and v1.14 for removing the alias.

behaviours.name: Stable sort of scored priorities
behaviours.note: Unreleased on Charon main. Only changes results for a tie among thirteen or more priorities in a topic, which no released Charon produces.

behaviours.name: Sender-bound share indices in the DKG lock-hash exchange
behaviours.note: Unreleased on Charon main. Rejects only partial signatures no honest peer sends.

behaviours.name: Strict cluster file validation (fixed-length fields, address checksums, lock deposit data and builder registrations)
behaviours.note: Not in Charon main at this anchor; Charon accepts most of the cluster_validation suite's rejected cases. Rejects only files Charon's DKG never writes.

test_vectors.description: BLS12-381 key derivation, signing, and both aggregations, over a fixed threshold-3-of-4 sharing. The shares are the evaluations of one degree-2 polynomial at x=1..4, so any three of them reconstruct the group key: threshold_aggregates therefore all equal group_signature, which is what distinguishes correct Lagrange coefficients from plausible ones. The scheme is BLS_SIG_BLS12381G2_XMD:SHA-256_SSWU_RO_POP_ (Ethereum, minimal-pubkey-size).

Config, definition and lock hashes of cluster configuration files at version v1.10.0. Each case's input is a verbatim charon cluster file, so 0x-prefixed hex inside input is charon's encoding; the expected hashes follow this directory's convention of bare lower-case hex. The definition group also pins the property the config hash exists for: adding signatures must not change it.

Which v1.10.0 cluster definitions and locks a reader MUST accept or reject. A definition is accepted if it parses under the field rules (fixed lengths, addresses, deposit amount bounds and sum) and its stored hashes match. A lock is accepted if it parses and passes the full verification sequence: hashes, public shares, deposit data, builder registrations, signature aggregate, node signatures (against node_pubkeys). Every rejected case breaks exactly one rule and is otherwise fully valid; length and address cases are hashed and signed over the value a lenient reader would decode (short fields left-padded as Charon pads them, the registration fee recipient right-padded, long fields truncated, addresses case-insensitive), so a reader that pads instead of rejecting finds every hash and signature valid.

A peer may only contribute a partial signature under the share index the cluster assigned it, resolved through a peer map rather than the peer's position: removing an operator leaves survivors with gapped indices, which is what breaks a position-derived implementation. Construction rejects a participant with no assigned index, since otherwise its signatures are dropped as unknown and the exchange silently times out.
Cluster-wide priority results for a topic, given each peer's proposed order. Every peer also proposes an empty 'ignored' topic, which must appear in the result with no priorities.

Once an instance has decided, a post-decision ROUND-CHANGE triggers at most one DECIDED rebroadcast per source per strictly-increasing round, capped at 16 per source. `rebroadcast[i]` is whether event i triggers one. Counted as rebroadcast events, not messages, since a rebroadcast reaches every peer.

Deterministic protobuf encodings and SSZ hash roots for the messages a Distributed Validator hashes: consensus values, duties, QBFT message signing roots, and the Any-wrapped strings the priority protocol uses.

Limits a receiver MUST apply to an incoming QBFT consensus message before any per-element work: justifications <= 2*nodes, values <= 2*(justifications+1), and a wire size of at most 33554432 bytes (32 MiB). Every case names the rejection reason, because agreeing on which limit fired is what makes the two checks distinguishable.

secp256k1 signatures in the 65-byte R || S || V form used for QBFT consensus messages, node signatures over the cluster lock hash, and cluster definition operator signatures. The nonce is RFC 6979 deterministic, so these bytes are reproducible exactly.
First-expiry deadlines of the eager double linear consensus round timer. deadline_nanos = genesis + slot_duration * slot + duty_start_delay + round_timeout, all in integer nanoseconds.
